description:
CLOSED-AS-REFUTED pending fz-kdt.125's landing (2026-09-01 review
verdict). This ticket asked whether kdt.106's row dominance should
compare captured-closure columns through their runtime-observable
erasure (fun_top) -- the same judgement fz-kdt.118 made for the
dispatch drop rule. The fz-kdt.125 review REFUTED THE PREMISE: the
erasure of callables to fun_top is itself the defect (closure values
carry identity at runtime; the predicate gains an identity axis), so
'compare through the erasure' inverts -- under the new axis the
observable form of a closure column IS its identity, and the proposed
relaxation would be a no-op at best, unsound at worst. The row
dominance's verbatim closure-shape guard (lit_arrow_shapes
containment) stays as-is: it is exactly identity-respecting, which is
now known to be the runtime-faithful comparison. The one standing
consequence (00277's FIFO Range.reduce pair with different captured
inner closures not absorbing) is correct behaviour under the new
understanding -- those rows ARE runtime-distinguishable. Close this
ticket when fz-kdt.125 lands and the 00277 pair re-measures under the
axis; nothing to build here.
title: REFUTED BY SEQUENCE: comparing callable columns through their runtime erasure inverts once the erasure itself is refuted
